reviews.title: Not what I was expecting
reviews.text: The app is buggy. Although it fairness so is the web site. Both the app and the website are near clones of each other. Navigation and response times are challenges. The big turn off for me is the subscription price, it’s outrageous . I was only looking to take one class. Coursera is no longer what it was a few years ago.

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.text:
The ICD-1o medical billing and coding course has the following issues: -missing documentation samples (Course 3 Module 2 of Superbill)
-missing mid-session prompt practice question (Course 2)
-Incorrect transcript versus what speaker actually said (multiple videos, including Course 3 Module 2 Superbill Components and Payer Integration
-Graded assignments with fill-in sections are marked incorrect when they are indeed correct (almost all graded quizes)
-Course 4 Module 1 Hands-On Coding Resource Navigation Workshop the first link does not work
-Missing Systematic coding worksheet in Course 4 Module 2: Code Real Clinical Scenarios assignment
-The entire four courses are repetitions of the same lessons. Could have been minimized to 2 courses maximum. 
-Key lessons and resources, such as how to look up different types of codes, are not introduced until after a few modules, making it difficult to complete the first few lessons. 
-I submitted a message to the community forum for help locating missing documents and I received no reply. I messaged Coursera directly through their website and received no reply. I then emailed them directly via an email I previously used for another issue and received no reply. 
Course 4 Module 2 Medical Billing Competency test has the answers displayed

reviews.title: No Support
reviews.text:
During my trail I decided to pay for 6 months. I had an issue with my payment. I reached out to support. They told me just be patient someone will reach out. No one did. The trail ended and my progress for that week is gone. 

And yet they are asking for $60/ month! When they can’t even respond in a timely matter. 

Don’t waste your time find alternatives. I advise universities to offer their courses elsewhere.

Update: almost 3 weeks later they responded with hey are you still having the issue. I said it’s been 3 weeks how do I trust you don’t mess up my progress in the future. The follow up email is: oh sorry you didn’t respond case closed. They took freaking three weeks and didn’t even give me a full day to respond. 

**** them. But yeah universities this is how they treat your courses.

reviews.title: Charged for wrong membership and refused issuing refund
reviews.text: Coursera asked me to take a plus membership to carry on my courses (locked ones) and after help center told me that these locked courses are not part of plus membership. They didn’t accept to refund the plus membership to allow me paying for the one I wanted to purchase. They practice scam technics to make you pay services you don’t want!!! Shame on you Coursera :(

reviews.title: ID verification process is completely broken
reviews.text: Completely maddening. Forces fake locks on content as if it’s being taught by an actual professor. “You can’t access this until x”. Just so you have to pay for multiple months of the subscription. ID verification is totally broken for iPhone. Camera control doesn’t work.  I’ve never seen an app this bad at taking a photo.

reviews.title: Poor quality app, customer service policies are very poor
reviews.text: The courses that I have tried are very basic and it’s hard to use on your phone. I tried to cancel after the free trial but they purposefully make it difficult to cancel.  When I emailed for assistance with cancelling, I was told to do it myself and the account was left open and I was charged for an additional two months despite repeat emails. Do not recommend!

reviews.title: Unable to cancel subscription
reviews.text: This is a complete scam. I opened a subscription the course was useless I tried to cancel it but their website and app did not show the subscription so I couldn’t. However they are charging me every month. The ‘help’ is simply a bot and is a useless waste of time.

reviews.title: Don’t cancel your subscription if you want a refund
reviews.text: They will rip you off and now refund you even if you forgot and didn’t use their service. They do not refund you even if you were in the hospital. This service ripped me off and it’s sinister and wrong. Do not subscribe.

reviews.title: BEWARE!!! Coursera STEALS! & You can not talk to an actual person for customer service
reviews.text:
I have been trying to cancel my Coursera subscription for the past six months as I do not use it that often. Each time I try to contact the help center on their website or app I am directed to a chat bot who never can adequately answer my questions or point me in the direction of who I can speak with that can help or give me any resources as to how I can solve my issue….. I have continuously been charged $49 a month even though on the app, it lists my subscription as inactive. And though they are taking money out of my account, which I have proof of , There is no accompanying receipt or documentation of the charges in my profile under payments. Also when I try to access my content which i should have access to because i am being charged for it, I am unable to use any of the courses… I have had to cancel my card. But the bigger issue is I have no way to request a refund for the charges for a service I have not been able to use…I am very disheartened by this service as on the surface it seems to be a great way to educate those who would usually not have access. But the way they steal and treat their customers has made them loose a one…..

please beware, and don’t end up like me, missing $300+ with nothing to show for it.

reviews.title: A lot to fix still
reviews.text: Reading material here is horrible, specially in the iPad where text go from margin to margin almost without any bleed (landscape mode is atrocious). Headings in readings are bad as well. On my iPhone looks better, probably because they only thought people will study in their phones or PCs. I study mostly in my iPad since I write on a notebook while studying and having the screen divided and watching a Coursera video is the worst, in portrait mode the subtitles are in the bottom while the video remains in the middle of the window, landscape is better for this. When using toggled (video hovers on top of your workspace) you don’t need subtitles so there isn’t any. Same with screen mirroring to the TV, need subtitles? Too bad. There’s also components that are only available in PC so there’s always a halt on your flow if you’re studying anywhere but in the computer. Texts are great to read in the computer so I know they can do better… the problem is my computer is zero comfortable to read or have with me on the go… Material is great, courses are great… Is the UX/UI that is lacking, probably because none of the developers actually studies in different devices and/or they don’t count with UX/UI designer. P.S. The new podcast/audio only for videos thing is a nice added feature. Improving little, improving dreadfully slow, but improving I guess…

reviews.title: Terrible service
reviews.text: I paid for a year of Plus membership. Beware that most of these courses don’t even have an instructor to give you grades. They often use “peer review” which means your assignment will be graded by two of your classroom peers. The problem with this is many of your peers will not give you a fair grade so you will not pass that assignment and have to start over and this is after you’ve waited potentially days for two people to even score your assignment in the first place. I’m currently waiting on a peer review assignment yet again just so I can get my certificate. I’ve reached out to the support team, but they just sent me AI responses. This is a terrible service and it is not worth the money.

reviews.title: Terrible

reviews.title: Dishonest Business Practices
reviews.text: It seems at first glance to be an unbeatable offer: a seven day free trial of the learning account, and with it a free three month trial to Google AI pro. However, when I got about three modules in, it came time to download the trial as advertised, for the Google AI pro. Upon trying to activate the Google trial that was bundled with Coursera, the activation failed, and it stated you must be using the paid version of Coursera. The offer un-clearly inferred that the trial to the AI pro was going to be part of the free trial. I did troubleshoot, and even spoke with customer service, and it turns out that the messaging, including the misleading claims of free trials, were intentional.. I was so looking forward to increasing my knowledge in several different areas, and seeing the bundled free trial offer was what finally convinced me that it was time to start paying for some more continuing education classes. After this incident, I find myself disheartened and disillusioned. I feel that there should be zero trickery when it comes to free trial fine print. We’re all used to dishonest business practices, but this one was especially hurtful.
